summary: pairwise yields overlapping adjacent pairs: positions zero and one, then one and two, and so on.
documentation: pairwise yields overlapping adjacent pairs: positions zero and one, then one and two, and so on. The output contains one fewer item than a nonempty input, and inputs shorter than two items produce no pairs.
returns: The signed change between each item and its immediate predecessor.
caution: Pairs overlap; this is not disjoint grouping or a Cartesian product. Materialize the calculated differences into a list for JSON output.
scenarios: Calculate changes between consecutive meter readings.
Measure gaps between ordered event counters.
Build a local sequence of day-to-day balance changes.
title: Calculate adjacent changes
problem: For input [a,b,c,...], return [b-a,c-b,...]. Preserve signs. Empty input and a single value return [].
hint: Import pairwise and subtract the first member of each pair from the second.
goal: Use itertools.pairwise() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
